subject: Urban Planning
title: The Flint Water Crisis
description: A quick win: understand The Flint Water Crisis.

hook.text: In 2014, Flint, Michigan switched water sources to save money. Lead poisoned 100,000 residents for 18 months.

buildup.text: The new source corroded old lead pipes. Officials knew but told residents the water was safe to drink.

discovery.text: Children's blood lead levels doubled. Lead causes permanent brain damage — there is no safe level for children.

twist.text: Flint is 57% Black and deeply impoverished. Experts say the crisis would never have happened in a wealthy white city.

climax.text: Criminal charges were filed against nine officials. Most had charges dropped. The pipes are still being replaced.

punchline.text: They poisoned a city to save $5 million. The cleanup cost $600 million.

quiz.question: Why did the Flint water crisis happen?
options: A natural disaster contaminated the city's main reservoir
A cost-cutting water source switch corroded old lead pipes
Industrial pollution leaked into the groundwater supply
